successors.name: Lavo Kingdom
successors.text: Lavapura and the lower Chao Phraya, from 648

successors.name: Suphannaphum Kingdom
successors.text: the western valley: Nakhon Pathom, U Thong and Khu Bua

successors.name: Khmer Empire
successors.text: Si Thep and its plain in Phetchabun, the eastern centre

ledger.x: 583: Dvaravati, a network of Mon-speaking polities in central Thailand, first appears in Chinese records.
648: the political centre moves to Lavapura.
913: the western valley passes to Suphannabhum.

wars.name: Angkorian conquest of Si Thep
wars.outcome: Angkor takes Si Thep in 946 and ends its line by 949.

certainty.note: The page names sites, not boundaries; Dvaravati is a network of polities and a cultural sphere that also reached Isan and lowland Laos from the 6th century without being one state.
